items.q: I used to clean and polish Mr. Thompson's horn for which he would pay me for doing it.

ctx.x: Another great musician I saw at Keith was a clarinettist by the name of Wilton Crawley. Crawley would put a glass of water on his forhead and do a slow summersault while playing his clarinet and never spill a drop of water from the glass. I also saw Rudy Weidoft who was known as the fastest executor on an alto saxophone in those times. There were also classical pianists that came to Keith's Theatre and one I remember had two very long grand pianos, one which was controlled by electricity and he played a…

There was a man living next door to me named Mr. Thompson who played trumpet and baritone horn in a band lead by Mr. Bert Ferguson who played trumpet. Mr. Ferguson came to Cincinnati around 1917 and formed a marching and concert band for the Knights of Pythians lodge. I used to clean and polish Mr. Thompson's horn for which he would pay me for doing it.

There were some buildings in Sinton Park that were used as a school for children and Bert Ferguson used to rehearse the band in one of these buildings. I went to many of these rehearsals with Mr. Thompson. If anyone played a wrong note in one of the numbers, Mr. Ferguson would tell just who had made the mistake and tell him what note it should be. It was very interesting to assist at these rehearsals because I loved to hear music.
